claims.text: DonHang.Api validates access tokens locally (signature, iss, aud, exp) without calling Keycloak, so it accepts a validly signed access token until it expires and cannot recall it earlier, even after a logout at Keycloak.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Api/Program.cs:37-51; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/refresh-token.txt last line (-> 200 after logout)

claims.text: The realm sets accessTokenLifespan 300: Keycloak writes exp = iat + 300 into access tokens, and expires_in in the token response is 300.
claims.source_hint: donhang-realm.json:5; refresh-token.txt output (exp - iat = 300, expires_in 300); Keycloak Admin Guide: Access Token Lifespan

claims.text: Program.cs sets no ClockSkew, so JwtBearer keeps the default 300 s leeway: a token is accepted up to about 5 minutes past exp, then rejected with 401. A leaked access token works for minutes, not days.
Keycloak's token response to the authorization code exchange contains a refresh_token alongside the access_token (and refresh_expires_in).
claims.source_hint: scripts/backend/refresh-token.sh:15-17 (jq .refresh_token); outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/refresh-token.txt; RFC 6749 §5.1 (refresh_token OPTIONAL in token response)

claims.text: A client renews with POST to the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, client_id and refresh_token (no password, no client secret for the public client donhang-app) and receives a new, different access token.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §6 (Refreshing an Access Token); scripts/backend/refresh-token.sh:30-35; output 'different from the first: yes', -> 200

claims.text: The renewed access token again has the realm's access token lifetime (300 s).
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Access Token Lifespan applies to every issued access token; keycloak/donhang-realm.json:5

claims.text: Keycloak issues a new access token for a refresh token only while the refresh token's user session is active; after logout the refresh request fails with error invalid_grant, 'Session not active'.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/refresh-token.txt ('renew again after logging out'); Keycloak Server Admin Guide: user sessions; RFC 6749 §5.2 invalid_grant

claims.text: The client sends the refresh token only to Keycloak: the token endpoint to renew and the openid-connect/logout endpoint (client_id + refresh_token) to end the session (204); then every refresh token of that session stops working.
claims.source_hint: scripts/backend/refresh-token.sh:38-45; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/refresh-token.txt (-> 204, then invalid_grant for the first refresh token); Keycloak docs: OIDC logout endpoint

claims.text: The refresh token sent to GET /api/v1/orders/1 in the Authorization header gets 401: its aud is the realm issuer, not donhang-api, and Keycloak signs it with a key (HS512) not among the public keys the API downloads.
claims.source_hint: refresh-token.txt (second call -> 401); Program.cs:48-50 (Audience donhang-api); decoded refresh token: alg HS512, typ Refresh, aud realm issuer

claims.text: ssoSessionIdleTimeout 1800: the session ends after about 1,800 s (Keycloak adds a two-minute margin) without sign-in or refresh; each refresh restarts it; ssoSessionMaxLifespan 36000: ends at latest 10 h after login. Both bound refresh tokens.
claims.source_hint: keycloak/donhang-realm.json:6-7; Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Session and token timeouts (SSO Session Idle, SSO Session Max)

claims.text: refresh_expires_in in the token response is 1800, equal to ssoSessionIdleTimeout in this realm.

DonHang.App at stage-2 keeps only the access token and never renews it; once the API answers 401 (a few minutes after exp), the customer signs in again through Keycloak, which skips the password while the session lasts.

refresh-token.sh: earlier lines sign in as customer 1, set $access_token/$refresh_token, then call the API once with each; $keycloak is the realm openid-connect address; call_api prints the status of GET /api/v1/orders/1; curl -d sends POST fields; jq -r reads a JSON field.

HTTPS protects a token only in transit; a copy taken from a log, a browser or a bug report stays valid for its whole lifetime, so long-lived access tokens widen the damage of a leak regardless of HTTPS.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §10.3, §10.4; RFC 6819 (OAuth threat model) on short-lived access tokens

claims.text: What a caller may do (realm roles, via the roles mapper with access.token.claim) travels in the access token, so a permission removed at Keycloak keeps working at the API until that access token expires.
claims.source_hint: outline backend.l2.role-based-access item 4; keycloak/donhang-realm.json:47-58 (roles mapper, access.token.claim)

claims.text: The renewal response (grant_type=refresh_token) also contains a new refresh token of the same session; the script sends that one to the logout endpoint and retries renewal with the first one.
claims.source_hint: scripts/backend/refresh-token.sh:30-45 (jq .refresh_token <<<$renewed); RFC 6749 §6 (MAY issue a new refresh token)

claims.text: A Keycloak realm holds one system's users, clients and settings; Đơn Hàng's realm donhang is imported from keycloak/donhang-realm.json. iat is the JWT claim for the time the token was issued.
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Core concepts (realm); keycloak/donhang-realm.json:2; RFC 7519 §4.1.6 (iat)
